explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. John, who is seeing these visions, is told, “Go and measure the temple of God and the altar, and count the number of worshipers there.” (Revelation 11:1) So it's a measuring job AND a headcount. I'd want a clipboard for that one.

Close, because the altar does get measured. But the text says John is to measure the temple of God and the altar, then count something else. It's the worshipers there (Revelation 11:1). Nobody's counting stones, thank goodness. That would take until the next batch of dough rose twice.

No gates come up in this part, friend. John is told to measure the temple of God and the altar. Then he's told to “…count the number of worshipers there.” (Revelation 11:1) The count is about people, not doors.

I see where you're headed, but the text gives a different reason. John is told, “Do not measure it, because it has been given over to the nations…” (Revelation 11:2) Nothing there says the courtyard is too holy. It says the courtyard has been given over to the nations.

That's right. The text says, “Do not measure it, because it has been given over to the nations…” (Revelation 11:2) So the reason is that the courtyard has been given over to the nations. It never says anything about being too holy to measure. When the Bible hands you the reason, you take the reason it hands you.
Yes, baker. The nations “…will trample the holy city for 42 months.” (Revelation 11:2) It's a time with a number on it. Trampling is walking heavily right over something.

Nope, nobody is rebuilding anything in this verse. The nations will trample the holy city for 42 months (Revelation 11:2). Trampling is the opposite of building. It's more like walking over the whole place.

I get why guard sounds right, since the courtyard was handed to somebody. But the text says the nations “…will trample the holy city for 42 months.” (Revelation 11:2) That's trampling, not guarding. A guard stands watch, and these folks stomp through.
That's right. The two witnesses will prophesy for 1,260 days, “…clothed in sackcloth.” (Revelation 11:3) Sackcloth is rough, plain cloth. That's a long stretch of days to wear it.
Fine linen sounds nice, but that's not what the text says. The witnesses will prophesy for 1,260 days, “…clothed in sackcloth.” (Revelation 11:3) Sackcloth is the opposite of fancy.

Camel's hair! You dressed those witnesses like you had a big budget and a lot of nerve. But this verse says the two witnesses will prophesy for 1,260 days, “…clothed in sackcloth.” (Revelation 11:3) No camel on that label, friend.
You got it. If anyone wants to harm the two witnesses, “…fire proceeds from their mouths and devours their enemies.” (Revelation 11:5) The text says it plainly. These two are protected.

Not quite. The text gives the fire a different job. It comes out of their mouths when anyone wants to harm them, and it “…devours their enemies.” (Revelation 11:5) Nothing in the verse says it purifies the city.

I like the picture, but that's not what this fire does. The text says it “…proceeds from their mouths and devours their enemies.” (Revelation 11:5) It comes out when someone wants to harm the witnesses. Lighting the temple isn't mentioned.

That's right. The two witnesses have “…power to shut the sky so that no rain will fall during the days of their prophecy…” (Revelation 11:6) The days of their prophecy is the stretch of time we just heard about. That's a lot of sky to be in charge of.
Actually, it's true. Verse 6 says these witnesses have “…power to shut the sky so that no rain will fall during the days of their prophecy…” (Revelation 11:6) The verse names the power right there.
Yes, baker. They have power “…to turn the waters into blood…” (Revelation 11:6) That's one big power, and it comes right alongside shutting the sky. Just reading it makes me want to check the faucet.
I wish this were the version with wine, friend, but it isn't. The text says the witnesses have power “…to turn the waters into blood…” (Revelation 11:6) Blood is the word the verse uses.
Oil is a fair guess, but it isn't in this verse. For the waters, verse 6 says they have power “…to turn the waters into blood…” (Revelation 11:6) So blood is the answer.

That's right. “…the beast that comes up from the Abyss will wage war with them…” (Revelation 11:7) The text says it plainly. This happens once the witnesses have finished their testimony. The beast is the one who comes up from the Abyss in this verse.

The dragon does show up in this book, in Revelation 12:3, but it isn't named here. Verse 7 says “…the beast that comes up from the Abyss will wage war with them…” (Revelation 11:7) So the beast is the one to remember for this verse.

The false prophet isn't named in this verse. The text says “…the beast that comes up from the Abyss will wage war with them…” (Revelation 11:7) The beast is our answer. Stick close to the verse and you'll stay safe.

Yes, baker. The beast “…will wage war with them, and will overpower and kill them.” (Revelation 11:7) I think this is a heavy part, and I'll say it plainly. But this verse isn't the end of the story, so hold on.

Actually, it's true. The text says the beast “…will wage war with them, and will overpower and kill them.” (Revelation 11:7) I think that's a heavy thing to read. We're staying with the text, and the text says the beast overpowers them.

That's right. Their bodies will lie in the street of the great city, “…where their Lord was also crucified.” (Revelation 11:8) The text gives that detail right alongside the city's figurative names, Sodom and Egypt. It's a sober line, so we'll keep it simple.
Not this time, friend. The text says the great city is where their Lord “…was also crucified.” (Revelation 11:8) Being born isn't mentioned in this verse. The verse names the crucifixion.
I can see why you'd pick it, but baptized isn't what the verse says. It says the great city is where their Lord “…was also crucified.” (Revelation 11:8) That's the word to hold on to.

explanations.answer: The bodies to be laid in a tomb
explanations.explanation: Right on, baker. For three and a half days, they “…will not permit them to be laid in a tomb.” (Revelation 11:9) That's the one thing the text says they refuse. I think it's a hard thing to picture, so we'll just move along gently.

explanations.answer: Anyone to mourn over the bodies
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't say anything about mourning. It says the nations “…will not permit them to be laid in a tomb.” (Revelation 11:9) So the refusal is about the burial. The verse doesn't go beyond that.

explanations.answer: Anyone to speak the prophets' names
explanations.explanation: Names don't come up in this verse. What it says is that the nations “…will not permit them to be laid in a tomb.” (Revelation 11:9) That's the answer. I'd stick to what's written.

That's right. Those who dwell on the earth “…will gloat over them and celebrate and send one another gifts…” (Revelation 11:10) The verse gives the reason too. It says these two prophets had tormented them.

It's actually true. The text says those who dwell on the earth “…will gloat over them and celebrate and send one another gifts…” (Revelation 11:10) The verse gives the reason too. It says these two prophets had tormented them.
That's right. They celebrate “…because these two prophets had tormented them.” (Revelation 11:10) The text gives the reason in the same breath. Plain and direct.

Ignored is a little softer than the text. It says the earth's people celebrate “…because these two prophets had tormented them.” (Revelation 11:10) The verse gives that as the reason. So tormented is the word.
Not forgotten, friend. The verse says they celebrate “…because these two prophets had tormented them.” (Revelation 11:10) Those are the words. It's the reason the text hands us.

explanations.answer: The breath of life from God
explanations.explanation: That's right! “…the breath of life from God entered the two witnesses, and they stood on their feet…” (Revelation 11:11) After three and a half days, the whole scene turns around. I love this verse. It reads like a plot twist that God wrote.

explanations.answer: A burning coal from the altar
explanations.explanation: A burning coal is a vivid picture, but the text doesn't say it. It says “…the breath of life from God entered the two witnesses…” (Revelation 11:11) That's what happens after the three and a half days. It's a different image, and a good one.

explanations.answer: A light from the throne of God
explanations.explanation: Nice guess, but that's not what the verse says. After the three and a half days, “…the breath of life from God entered the two witnesses…” (Revelation 11:11) So it's breath, not light. And they stood on their feet right after.
Not quite, friend. When they stand on their feet, “…great fear fell upon those who saw them.” (Revelation 11:11) So the watchers aren't cheering. The text says fear fell on them.

That's right. The text says “…they stood on their feet, and great fear fell upon those who saw them.” (Revelation 11:11) No cheering is mentioned. After all that celebrating, I think the mood changes fast.

explanations.answer: Up to heaven in a cloud
explanations.explanation: That's right. The witnesses hear a loud voice from heaven say, “Come up here.” And “…they went up to heaven in a cloud as their enemies watched them.” (Revelation 11:12) Their enemies are watching as it happens. I'd love to see their faces.
No, they don't go back into the city. The text says they heard “Come up here.” and “…they went up to heaven in a cloud as their enemies watched them.” (Revelation 11:12) It's up, not back.

The wilderness isn't in this verse. After the loud voice says “Come up here.” “…they went up to heaven in a cloud as their enemies watched them.” (Revelation 11:12) The direction is up. That's what the verse says.
That's right. In the great earthquake, “…a tenth of the city collapsed.” (Revelation 11:13) It happens in the same hour the witnesses go up. The text gives the fraction, and we keep it exactly.

A third does show up elsewhere in this book (Revelation 8:7), but not in this verse. Here the text says “…a tenth of the city collapsed.” (Revelation 11:13) So tenth is the word. Always check which verse you're standing in.
Half would be a lot bigger. The text says “…a tenth of the city collapsed.” (Revelation 11:13) So it's a tenth. Fractions matter, friend. Ask anybody who's ever cut a batch of dough.

explanations.answer: They are terrified and give glory to God
explanations.explanation: That's right. After the earthquake, “…the rest were terrified and gave glory to the God of heaven.” (Revelation 11:13) I think that's a big shift after all the gloating earlier. The text puts the terror and the glory together in one breath.

explanations.answer: They curse God and refuse to repent
explanations.explanation: That's not what happens here. The text says the rest “…were terrified and gave glory to the God of heaven.” (Revelation 11:13) They give glory to God in this verse. It's a quiet turn.

explanations.answer: They flee to the mountains and hide
explanations.explanation: The mountains aren't in this verse. The text says the rest “…were terrified and gave glory to the God of heaven.” (Revelation 11:13) So giving glory is the answer.

explanations.answer: The world's kingdom has become the Lord's
explanations.explanation: That's right! The voices say, “The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of His Christ…” (Revelation 11:15) The seventh trumpet brings this announcement. That's the big news of the whole passage.

explanations.answer: The holy city has been measured again
explanations.explanation: Measuring was John's job back in verse 1, and it doesn't come back here. The voices call out, “The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of His Christ…” (Revelation 11:15) That's the announcement. Put the measuring rod down, friend.

explanations.answer: The great city has been rebuilt for good
explanations.explanation: Rebuilding isn't what the voices announce. They say, “The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of His Christ…” (Revelation 11:15) The announcement is about a kingdom, not a building project.
That's right. The voices go on, “…and He will reign forever and ever.” (Revelation 11:15) Forever and ever. That's the last word of the announcement.

It's actually true. The voices in heaven say, “The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of His Christ, and He will reign forever and ever.” (Revelation 11:15) Their announcement ends with forever and ever.

explanations.answer: Fall on their faces and worship God
explanations.explanation: That's right. The twenty-four elders “…who sit on their thrones before God fell on their faces and worshiped God…” (Revelation 11:16) They respond by worshiping. That's a good example to follow.

explanations.answer: Stand up and sound their own trumpets
explanations.explanation: The trumpet in this passage is sounded by the seventh angel, not the elders. The elders sit on their thrones and “…fell on their faces and worshiped God…” (Revelation 11:16) So they go down, not up. It's a quieter move than a trumpet.

explanations.answer: Rise and leave their thrones in fear
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't say they leave. It says the twenty-four elders “…fell on their faces and worshiped God…” (Revelation 11:16) They worship, and fear isn't named as the reason. So we leave fear out of it.
That's right. The elders say, “…because You have taken Your great power and have begun to reign.” (Revelation 11:17) That's their reason for giving thanks. They say it right to Him.

Measuring was John's assignment back in verse 1, not what the elders thank God for. They say, “…because You have taken Your great power and have begun to reign.” (Revelation 11:17) That's the reason. Nice try, though.

Sealing thunders doesn't come up in the elders' words. They say, “…because You have taken Your great power and have begun to reign.” (Revelation 11:17) So the reason for their thanks is that He has begun to reign.
That's right. The elders say, “The time has come to judge the dead…” (Revelation 11:18) It's right there in their words. Heavy words, so I'll say it simply and move on.
Mourn isn't the word they use. The elders say, “The time has come to judge the dead…” (Revelation 11:18) The word is judge. We'll hold on to that.
Count was John's job back in verse 1, when he was told to count the worshipers. Here the elders say, “The time has come to judge the dead…” (Revelation 11:18) So this time the word is judge.

That's not quite what the elders say. They say the time has come “…to reward Your servants the prophets, as well as the saints and those who fear Your name, both small and great…” (Revelation 11:18) The prophets are named first, but they're not the only ones. The reward goes further than that.

That's right. The elders say the time has come “…to reward Your servants the prophets, as well as the saints and those who fear Your name, both small and great…” (Revelation 11:18) The prophets are named, and so are the saints and those who fear His name. The word only doesn't fit, so there's room at the table for more.

explanations.answer: To destroy those who destroy the earth
explanations.explanation: That's right. The elders finish by saying it's time “…to destroy those who destroy the earth.” (Revelation 11:18) That's the last thing on their list. I'm sticking with their exact words.

explanations.answer: To gather the nations to the city
explanations.explanation: Gathering isn't on the elders' list. They say the time has come “…to destroy those who destroy the earth.” (Revelation 11:18) Their words are about destroying. Everything else on their list is judging and rewarding.

explanations.answer: To seal the servants of God
explanations.explanation: Sealing is not in the elders' words. They say the time has come “…to destroy those who destroy the earth.” (Revelation 11:18) That's their last item. Keep close to what they actually say.

That's right. When God's temple in heaven was opened, “…the ark of His covenant appeared in His temple.” (Revelation 11:19) The text puts the ark's appearing right there. I'll just let that line sit there.
A book is a good guess in this part of Revelation, but it isn't here. The text says “…the ark of His covenant appeared in His temple.” (Revelation 11:19) The ark is what appears.
A sign appears elsewhere in Revelation, in Revelation 12:1, but not in this verse. Here “…the ark of His covenant appeared in His temple.” (Revelation 11:19) So the word we need is ark.

That's right. When the temple opens, “…there were flashes of lightning, rumblings, peals of thunder, an earthquake, and a great hailstorm.” (Revelation 11:19) Lightning, thunder and hail are all in that list. Quite a finish for the whole passage, baker.

explanations.answer: Silence for about half an hour
explanations.explanation: That silence is real, but it belongs to a different moment. Revelation 8:1 says there was silence in heaven for about half an hour. Here, the opened temple comes with “…flashes of lightning, rumblings, peals of thunder, an earthquake, and a great hailstorm.” (Revelation 11:19) This verse is loud, friend.

A rainbow around the throne does show up in this book, in Revelation 4:3. As someone whose favorite color is the rainbow, I get why you picked it. But when the temple opens here, it's “…flashes of lightning, rumblings, peals of thunder, an earthquake, and a great hailstorm.” (Revelation 11:19) So no rainbow in this one.
